To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
water increases the rate of dermal absorption of water-miscible chemicals.
water mixtures of glycol ethers enhance dermal absorption.
glycol ethers penetrate human skin up to 6 fold more rapidly from aqueously dilute solutions than from neat solvent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dermal absorption and toxicity of chemicals.
the development of a new method for the measurement of dermal absorption of chemicals.
the influence of water on the dermal permeability of butoxyethanal and ethoxyethanal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glycol ethers in aqueous mixtures penetrate human skin at rates which are greater than neat solvent and that the rate of absorption increases as the concentration of glycol ether in water decreases.
the presence of water in the skin or in the formulation increases the absorption of glycol ether solvents.

the dermal absorption potential of glycol ether solvents is influenced by water mixtures, and that the effect is dependent on the solvent, its concentration in the water mixture, the water content of the mixture and the nature of the skin barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

glycol ethers penetrate more rapidly from aqueons solutions than from neat solvents, that this effect is more pronounced with butoxyethanol than with ethoxyethanol, and that absorption through a synthetic membrane obeys Fick's Law.
the absorption of water miscible solvents through human skin is influenced by the presence of water in the solvent mixture.
water mixtures of butoxyethanols and ethoxyethanols increase the rate of dermal absorption through human skin, synthetic membrane, and rat skin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
absorption of glycol ether solvents is influenced by the solvent-water ratio and the presence of water can increase absorption rates.
the dermal penetration of glycol ethers is increased when applied in a water-mixture and this should be considered in risk assessment of occupational exposure.

the presence of water can significantly increase the dermal penetration of glycol ethers and that risk assessment of dermally applied glycol ethers should ideally be based upon the relevant formulation or water mixtures and not neat solvent.
